correctness.rationale: For a multilinear noncommutative polynomial, evaluation on arbitrary matrices is determined by evaluation on the four matrix units. The evaluation map on the \(8!\) words therefore has a binary matrix with \(4^8\cdot4=262144\) scalar rows and 40320 columns. The package constructs every column by the unique matrix-unit path rule and performs exact bit Gaussian elimination. I inspected both independent C++ eliminators, which use opposite pivot orders, and the low-degree Python cross-check. A fresh compilation/run of the forward rank-eight program in this audit produced cumulative ranks 1246, 2492, 3456, 4029, 4313, 4432, 4474, 4487 and final rank 4487. Since the matrix entries lie in \(\mathbf F_2\), scalar extension to any characteristic-two field preserves rank.
risks: The reverse-pivot implementation was inspected but not separately rerun during this audit; the forward exact replay and independent algorithmic structure provide the numerical certificate.
